name: FrogNano-4B-2609

lineage.how_derived: reinforcement learning only on about 1,500 synthetic software-engineering tasks generated, validated and calibrated against the evolving policy with TaskPilot (five iterations), run through the five-tool Leaf harness; no stronger-model trajectories, actions, reasoning traces or patch targets

purpose: A compact repository-level coding agent for software-engineering research and human-supervised development: issue resolution, navigation, debugging, edits and test runs via Leaf tool calls. Microsoft calls it a research artifact; it is not a general assistant.

Python.evidence: training data Python-heavy; SWE-bench Verified Avg@3 61.5 % with the Leaf harness (vendor)

JavaScript.evidence: SWE-bench Pro (Python, JS, TS, Go) 37.6 % Avg@3 vendor, no per-language split on the card

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: Card header and the summary table state Apache-2.0 (derived from Qwen3.5-4B, upstream notices retained). The LICENSE file itself was not opened. A community GGUF repo is tagged MIT, which differs from the card.

architecture.kind: dense hybrid Gated DeltaNet + gated attention (Qwen3.5-4B)
architecture.attention: Gated DeltaNet / gated full attention hybrid inherited from Qwen3.5-4B; vision components inherited but untrained and unsupported
architecture.drafter: none stated (community MLX builds mention an MTP head; not verified)
architecture.why_this_design: The architecture is unchanged from Qwen3.5-4B; the card describes only the training approach (policy-calibrated synthetic environments, RL without teacher trajectories).

variants.notes: Q5_K_M 3.36, Q6_K 3.76, Q8_0 4.62, bf16 8.67, mmproj 0.68; also mradermacher GGUF and MLX builds

pc-16gb.notes: 131K context KV on top of 8.7 GB

engine_support.notes: Qwen3.5 architecture; the vendor's rollouts used SGLang. Tona runs the 35B-A3B Qwen3.5 MoE relatives, a dense 4B Qwen3.5 variant would need the dense path of that architecture.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified
benchmarks.variant: BF16, Leaf harness, 150 steps, 131K context, temperature 0.6

strengths: Largest coding-agent gain per parameter in the database for a 4B model (vendor: 39.4 to 61.5 % SWE-bench Verified with the same harness)
No distillation from a stronger model, so no inherited license or terms issue from a teacher
weaknesses: Performance sensitive to the Leaf harness and test quality
All scores vendor-run in the vendor's own harness; not evaluated for general language use
soft.behavior: Emits structured Leaf tool calls (read, write, edit, glob, shell); a response without a tool call ends the episode. Recommended temperature 0.6, repetition penalty 1.0; one user reports slight looping.
best_for: small coding-agent worker for Python repositories
research on RL for SWE agents
avoid_for: non-Python or non-English projects until measured

user_reports.summary: Performs very well for its size, sometimes loops slightly

soft.maturity: Microsoft research release with technical report and open Leaf harness; bartowski GGUF has 15k downloads; few discussions.

tona_fit.reason: A 4B coding agent is attractive as a fast sub-agent worker and for 12 GB cards, and the Apache-2.0 license is clean, but the evidence is vendor-only in a custom harness and Python-only; our Rust/Go eval has not been run. Candidate for a measured run with our harness before any offer.
blockers: vendor numbers in Leaf harness only
dense Qwen3.5 path not implemented in Tona

sources.note: discussion text via the HF API

open_questions: Independent reproduction of the SWE-bench numbers outside the Leaf harness
Rust, Go and JavaScript performance (card says Python-heavy)
LICENSE file text (card says Apache-2.0; community GGUF tagged MIT)
Quality loss at Q4_K_M and with KV quantization at 131K context
Whether an MTP head is present (community MLX repos suggest it)
